content.text:
The campaign ran Sunday Jan 3 through Wednesday Jan 6, Singapore time, and has ended on schedule. It spent **US$194.42** of the US$200 budget and got **484,673 impressions** and **545 link clicks**, about **US$0.36 per click**.

| Ad group | Spend | Impressions | Link clicks | Cost per click |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Parenting + Workouts interests | $119.62 | 263,911 | 366 | $0.33 |
| Pregnancy keywords | $74.81 | 220,762 | 179 | $0.42 |
| **Total** | **$194.42** | **484,673** | **545** | **$0.36** |

**By post (both ad groups combined):**
- **"Try 14 days for $0… US$9.99/month":** 189 clicks at $0.35. This one did best in the interests group.
- **Main post, "Pregnant and setting a 2027 resolution?":** 195 clicks at $0.36
- **"Only until January 6…":** 161 clicks at $0.37

**Setup:** one campaign with two ad groups, each running all three of your approved posts. Both ad groups were set to get as many link clicks as possible, since X can't see trial starts without the pixel. Both reached iPhone users only and excluded Russia and Belarus. After the first day the interests group was getting cheaper clicks, so I moved budget to it: $30 a day for interests and $20 a day for keywords, with combined caps that kept the total at $200. All posts were approved by X and nothing was rejected.

**Limits to keep in mind:**
- **English speakers only.** You only gave me the English versions of the posts, so I limited both ad groups to people using X in English. That left out your non-English audience, even though you have localized posts and pages for them. I should have told you this at launch instead of only now.
- **Not only pregnant people.** The interest group targeted parenting and workout interests broadly, so it reached many people who aren't pregnant. Its cheaper clicks may not turn into more trials.
- **Clicks aren't trials.** Compare your own trial-start count for Jan 3–6 with these 545 clicks to see the real cost per trial.
